title: para fazermos
summary: the personal infinitive: a dictionary form with an ending
intro: Portuguese can add endings to the infinitive to show who is doing it: *falar*, *falares*, *falar*, *falarmos*, *falarem*. English and Spanish can't do this.

Use it after words like *para*, *sem*, *antes* de, *depois* de, *até* and ao, and after *é melhor* or *é preciso*, when you want to say who: *É melhor irmos* = We'd better go. *Antes de saíres*, *fecha a janela* = Before you go out, close the window.

examples.pt: Antes de saíres, fecha a janela.
examples.en: Before you go out, close the window.
I brought this for you to see.

notes: It's never irregular: fazeres, *irmos*, sermos, termos.
Obrigado *por teres vindo* and Obrigado *por me teres* ajudado are very natural ways to thank someone.
For regular verbs it looks like the future subjunctive (*quando chegares*, *antes de chegares*). Irregular verbs show the difference: *quando fores* (subjunctive), *antes de ires* (infinitive).

drills.en: Before you go out, close the window.
I brought this for you to see.
After we have dinner, we'll go to the cinema.
When you get home, call me.

drills.why: After por comes an infinitive; with *tu* it's *teres*.
After *antes* de: the personal infinitive (*ires*). *Fores* is the future subjunctive, used after *quando* or se.

title: para leres, para que leias
summary: two ways to say the same thing
intro: After *para*, *sem*, *antes* de and *até* you can often choose: the personal infinitive (*para leres*) or que + subjunctive (*para que leias*). Both mean "so that you read".
In everyday Portugal the personal infinitive is more common, because it's shorter.

examples.en: I'm bringing the book for you to read.

examples.pt: Trago o livro para que o leias.
examples.en: The same, a little more formal.

examples.pt: Não saias sem levares o casaco.
examples.en: Don't go out without taking your coat.

notes: Some words only take the subjunctive: *embora*, *talvez*, *caso*. Ao only takes the infinitive: *ao chegares* (when you arrive).

drills.en: I'm bringing the book for you to read.

drills.before: Trago o livro para que o
drills.en: I'm bringing the book so that you can read it.
Don't go out without taking your coat.
I'll explain so that you understand.
I'll explain so that you understand.
Take the umbrella in case it rains.
Speak louder so that we can hear.
drills.why: After *para* comes the infinitive, here with the *nós* ending.
